items.title: A solution containing a purely inseparable degree p step can be replaced by a separable solution
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a prime p, an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction field extension L/K, and a tower K_2/K_1/K of finite extensions, assumes K of characteristic p, L/K separable, B Nagata, K_2 a solution for A in B, and K_2/K_1 purely inseparable of degree p, and concludes the existence of a separable extension K_3/K_1 which is a solution (source lines 35774-35788). The proof is a substantial construction. It first records that L_1 and L_2 are reduced, that the integral closures A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2 are finite and Nagata, and that pi is a nonzerodivisor with the four fraction field identifications (proof lines 35791-35808). It then writes K_2 = K_1(alpha) with alpha^p = a_1 in A_1 after multiplying alpha by a power of pi, and introduces the presentation algebras A'_2 = A_1[x]/(x^p - a_1) and B'_2 = B_1[x]/(x^p - a_1), to which the extension-construction lemma is applied at f = pi^2, yielding an integer n that works for both (proof lines 35809-35822). The genuine content is the deformation: it replaces x^p - a_1 by the etale algebras K_3 = K_1[x]/(x^p - pi^{2n} x - a_1) and L_3 = L_1[x]/(x^p - pi^{2n} x - a_1) together with the subrings A'_3 and B'_3 defined by x^p - pi^n x - a_1, builds the displayed commutative diagram of quotient algebras, and transports the chosen n back to get finite extensions A'_3 in A_3 and B'_3 in B_3 with A_3 -> B_3 extending A'_3 -> B'_3 and an isomorphism of the pi^2-quotients (proof lines 35825-35862). It then shows A_3 and B_3 are finite products of Dedekind domains with pi in every maximal ideal, that every maximal ideal of A_3 becomes principal in its localization by Nakayama, and hence that A_3 and B_3 are the integral closures of A and B in K_3 and L_3 (proof lines 35865-35876). The last step verifies the formal smoothness criterion using the pi^2-quotient isomorphism and the hypothesis that K_2 is a solution, with the author noting that some details are omitted (proof lines 35877-35889). The etale deformation and the Dedekind-product analysis are independent research-level content.
